en.location: 📍 Around Earnewâld (Eernewoude), between Leeuwarden, Drachten and Heerenveen — visitor centre at the Prinsehôf
en.description: The largest continuous nature area of the Frisian mainland and its youngest national park (2006): nearly 4,000 ha of low-fen marsh born from 17th-century peat dredging. A labyrinth of petgaten, legakkers, reed lands, trilveen (quaking bog), marsh woods and open plassen — with the Prinsehôf at its watery heart, the reed island-villages of the "koude hoek", monumental spinnekop mills (De Ikkers, Princehofmolen), a stork station (Eibertshiem) and, since recent years, a breeding pair of white-tailed eagles. Some 450 plant species and 100+ breeding birds; best explored by canoe, whisper boat or the ferry lines.
en.meta: Best Season & Peak Months: Apr–Jun (breeding) & Sep–Oct (reed harvest); May–Sep canoe season Best Time of Day: Dawn paddle — mist between the reed walls; evening otter hours.
en.natura2000: 🇪🇺 Natura 2000 De Alde Feanen — site 13, NL3009001 (Habitat- & Vogelrichtlijn), largely a National Park since 2006, managed chiefly by It Fryske Gea. Habitats: H3150 natural eutrophic lakes with pondweeds, H7140 transition mires & quaking bog (trilveen — the Hoannekrite near Earnewâld is botanically richest), H6410 purple-moor-grass meadows incl. blue grassland, H91D0 bog woodland (birch scrub with sweet gale at Brêgeham). Flagships: bittern, purple heron, great white egret, great reed warbler, white-tailed eagle; otter; the Netherlands' key Northern vole (Noordse woelmuis) population on the islands; pond bat foraging over the waterways.
why_visit: White-tailed eagle over the reed at Prinsehôf — Friesland's big comeback story.
The quaking-bog islands and flower-rich Hoannekrite (guided access).
Monumental mills, the stork station of Eibertshiem, and canoe routes through 300 years of peat history.
periodic_phenomena: Apr–Jun 🎶 Reed-bed chorus: bittern booming, great reed warblers, Savi's warbler.
Dec–Feb 🪿 Thousands of geese & ducks; otter tracks in frost mud.
Sep–Oct 🌾 Reed cutting — the working landscape at its most photogenic.
wildlife: 🌿 450 plant species incl. orchids on trilveen
trailheads: Visitor centre Skutsje út Ljekte / Earnewâld pop-up info point; the Prinsehôf landing; De Feanhoop (no. 200) for the south rim.
Canoe & whisper-boat rentals at Earnewâld and Wergea; ferry "de Alde Feanen fart" in summer.
en.footer: 🐶 Dogs on leash, prohibited in core reed beds Mar–Jul · 💶 Free; canoe/boat rental & pont charges apply · ⚠️ Boating only on marked routes in the breeding season

nl.location: 📍 Rond het watertje-dorp De Feanhoop (De Veenhoop), op de zuidrand van Nationaal Park De Alde Feanen
nl.description: De wildste hoek van de Alde Feanen, bereikt vanuit een dorp dat zelf één lange steiger is. Vier It Fryske Gea-complexen — Petgatten De Feanhoop (59 ha gebaggerde veenslagen), Noarderkrite (21 ha trilveen-riet), Kraanlannen en Oskekop — vormen een labyrint van smal open water, dichtgegroeide legakkers en soortenrijk riet, waar de veenmakers een eeuw geleden ophielden. Reigers, bruine kiekendieven en ijsvogels bewerken de slagen; de zwarte-stern-vlonders dobberen aan de randen.
nl.meta: Beste seizoen & piekmaanden: mei–jun (broedende rietvogels); sep (riet & paddenstoelen) Beste tijd van de dag: Dageraad vanaf de steigers; avondkano.
nl.natura2000: 🇪🇺 Ligt op/tegen de zuidrand van Nationaal Park De Alde Feanen (Natura 2000-gebied 13): de petgatten en rietlanden zetten de trilveen- en rietkwaliteiten (H7140) van het park voort; beheer door It Fryske Gea.
why_visit: Het dorp De Feanhoop zelf: cafés aan het water, kanoverhuur, het veer naar Earnewâld.
Rietvogels op armlengte: waterral, porseleinhoen (schraal), baardmannetje in de winter.
Geleide IFG-excursies het gesloten trilveen op.
trailheads: Park bij de haven van De Feanhoop; kijk vanaf de veersteiger & paddle de gemarkeerde kanoroutes.
nl.footer: 🐶 Honden aan de lijn · 💶 Gratis (kanoverhuur betaald) · ⚠️ Kern-petgatten gesloten — kijk vanaf water & steigers

en.location: 📍 Around the water village of De Feanhoop (De Veenhoop), on the southern rim of National Park De Alde Feanen
en.description: The wildest corner of the Alde Feanen, reached from a village that is itself one long jetty. Four It Fryske Gea complexes — Petgatten De Feanhoop (59 ha of dredged peat cuts), Noarderkrite (21 ha of quaking reed), Kraanlannen and Oskekop — form a labyrinth of narrow open water, overgrown legakkers and species-rich reed where the peat diggers left off a century ago. Herons, marsh harriers and kingfishers work the cuts; the black tern rafts bob at the edges.
en.meta: Best Season & Peak Months: May–Jun (breeding reed birds); Sep (reed & fungi) Best Time of Day: Dawn from the jetties; evening canoe.
en.natura2000: 🇪🇺 Lies on/against the southern rim of National Park De Alde Feanen (Natura 2000 site 13): the petgatten and reed lands continue the park's H7140 quaking-bog and reed-bed qualities; management by It Fryske Gea.
why_visit: De Feanhoop village itself: cafés on the water, canoe rental, the ferry to Earnewâld.
Reed birds at arm's length: water rail, spotted crake (scarce), bearded tit in winter.
Guided IFG excursions onto the closed quaking bogs.
periodic_phenomena: Nov–Feb 🐦‍⬛ Bearded tit flocks in the seed heads.
trailheads: Park at De Feanhoop harbour; view from the ferry jetty & paddle the marked canoe routes.
en.footer: 🐶 Dogs on leash · 💶 Free (canoe rental paid) · ⚠️ Core petgatten closed — view from water & jetties
